hints: Notice the y-axis is speed, the magnitude $\sqrt{v_x^2+v_y^2}$, not vertical velocity, and the path is symmetric over horizontal ground.
Connect the motion to physics: horizontal velocity $v_x$ stays constant while vertical velocity $v_y$ decreases to zero at the top and then grows downward.
Ask why the minimum speed cannot be zero and why the decrease and increase must be curved rather than straight lines.
walkthrough: Identify the components: with negligible air resistance, horizontal velocity $v_x$ is constant and vertical velocity is $v_y = u_y - gt$, which is positive on the way up, zero at the top, and negative on the way down.
State the rule for speed: speed is the magnitude $v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2}$, so only the size of $v_y$ matters, not its direction.

Follow the flight: after launch $|v_y|$ shrinks so $v$ decreases, at the top $v_y = 0$ so $v = |v_x|$ which is greater than zero, then $|v_y|$ grows so $v$ increases again to its launch value on landing.

Explain the shape: because of the square root and the $gt$ term, $v$ against $t$ is a curved U-shape with minimum above zero and with slope that is steepest at launch and landing and flattest at the top.
Match to the graphs: only the U-shaped curve that starts high, stays well above zero, and rises again fits this behaviour. This is option C.

A.explanation: Speed is not constant because the vertical component of velocity changes under gravity even though the horizontal component is constant.

B.explanation: Speed does not change linearly to zero because speed is $\sqrt{v_x^2+v_y^2}$ and the horizontal speed $v_x$ never becomes zero.

C.explanation: Speed decreases to a non-zero minimum at the top where only horizontal velocity remains, then increases symmetrically with a curved U-shape.

D.explanation: Speed never reaches zero at the top of the path because the horizontal component of velocity is unchanged when air resistance is negligible.
